title: When the Prompt Becomes Visual: Vision-Centric Jailbreak Attacks for Large Image Editing Models
benchmark_measurement: The benchmark, IESBench, measures the vulnerability of large image editing models to 'Discrimination-based Visual Editing' attacks. This category (I14) is defined as image editing operations that 'introduce, amplify, or reinforce discriminatory, hateful, or demeaning visual representations toward a protected class, including but not limited to race, ethnicity, nationality, religion, gender, sexual orientation, disability, or immigration status'.
findings: The paper does not provide findings specific only to religion. However, for the broader category of 'Discrimination-based Visual Editing' (which includes religion as a protected class), it found high attack success rates against various models. For example, Vision-Centric Jailbreak Attacks (VJA) achieved an Attack Success Rate (ASR) of 100.0% against Qwen-Image-Edit, 83.8% against Nano Banana Pro, and 82.4% against GPT Image 1.5 for this category, demonstrating a significant vulnerability to generating discriminatory content.
